description: What a headless build log redacts (PL.core-build-log-redaction; U115(11), U49(3): core is the source), so every engine's build log redacts the same things: a private-key block, a credential-key assignment (NAME=value, export NAME="value"), credentials anywhere in a line (the shapes secret-in-request refuses), and local paths (project-relative inside the project, <home> for a home folder, <user> for the user name as a path segment). Line in, line out; lines that must not change are cases too.
sources: core src/build/build-log-redaction.ts (redactBuildLogLine, redactBuildLog, redactCredentialAssignment, redactCredentialTokens, redactLocalPaths)
core src/build/headless-build.ts (isSecretKey, looksLikeSecret, BUILD_SECRET_KEY_STAND_IN) and conformance/build/headless.json contract.rules.credentials
core docs/headless-build.md § "What a build log redacts"
Unreal Source/InsimulEditor/Portable/InsimulBuildBinding.cpp FBuildRows::RedactCredentialAssignment (the interim rule, U106(1); unreal 16633f20)

rules.order: each line on its own, in this order: (1) a private-key block, (2) a credential-key assignment, (3) credentials anywhere in the line, (4) local paths. A line with nothing to redact comes back byte for byte; no line that comes out holds a credential by headless.json contract.rules.credentials's shapes. As many lines out as in
rules.privateKey: a line holding -----BEGIN <WORD >PRIVATE KEY----- is withheld whole (secretKeyStandIn); in a log (redactLog, or a runner carrying the state from line to line) so is every later line up to and including the one holding -----END <WORD >PRIVATE KEY-----, unless that footer follows the header on the header's own line
rules.assignment: at the line's FIRST =, when that is not its first character: the name is the [A-Za-z0-9_]+ run just before it, not starting with a digit, and everything before the name trimmed of spaces and tabs is nothing or exactly export. The value is everything after the =, trimmed (spaces and tabs at the start; spaces, tabs and a carriage return at the end), with one pair of enclosing double quotes removed. An empty value is kept. When the name is a credential key (headless.json contract.rules.credentials: lower-cased with toLowerCase, without _ and -, ending in one of its words) or the value holds a credential, the line becomes everything up to and including that =, then secretKeyStandIn. Names are ASCII. Anything else (NAME = value, set NAME=value, -flag=value mid-line, a second assignment on the line) is not an assignment: its value goes only by its shape, in (3)
rules.credentials: every span in the line that is a credential by headless.json contract.rules.credentials's shapes (a JWT, a database URL, a URL with user:password, Bearer and its token, a model or cloud key shape), run on to the end of its word (up to whitespace, a quote, a backtick, < or >), is secretKeyStandIn
rules.paths: in this order, each comparing as spelt: (a) context.projectDir, without trailing separators and unused when empty: where it is a whole path (not preceded by a path name character, and followed by a separator or a character that is not one), it and the one separator after it go, so the path reads project-relative, the form a build result names its artefacts in; alone it is projectStandIn. (b) context.homeDir the same way is homeStandIn. (c) a home folder by its usual form is homeStandIn, whoever's it is, at the start of an absolute path: the root folder Users or home (the folder word in any case) then a name (POSIX), or a drive letter, a colon, a separator, Users (any case) and a separator, then a name (Windows), unless the name is one of sharedHomeNames (ignoring ASCII case). A POSIX name runs to a separator; a Windows name may hold spaces and runs to the next separator or quote when one comes before a colon, else to whitespace. The Windows form is applied first. (d) context.userName where it is a whole path segment (after a separator, and followed by a separator, the end, or a character that is not a path name character) is userStandIn; never in prose. A path name character is an ASCII letter or digit, ., _, -, or anything outside ASCII. Relative paths are kept as spelt, so an outDir-relative path stays readable. A / before an absolute path is allowed (a file URL's third slash)
rules.runner: an engine redacts every line of its build log (logFile) and every logs[].message and progress message before it writes them, carrying the private-key state across one log. A runner that cannot answer the rule for a line (a row unanswered) withholds the line rather than passing it on
rules.secrets: a string holding <<secret:NAME>> stands for secretFixtures[NAME] joined; a runner expands every marker in input before answering. No expected line holds a credential
rules.local: a string holding <<local:NAME>> stands for localFixtures[NAME] joined: the start of a local home path, kept out of the file so no vendored corpus names a home folder as itself. Unlike secret markers, local markers appear in input AND expected; a runner expands both before it compares
